title: LSASS memory accessed with full-access masks by PowerShell (scranton) and wsmprovhost (nashua) under pbeesly
rationale: All describe the same LSASS handle events: PowerShell.exe PID 2976 on scranton.dmevals.local opening lsass.exe with 0x1f3fff/0x1fffff at 2020-05-02T03:05:16Z and wsmprovhost.exe PID 7720 on nashua.dmevals.local with 0x1f3fff at 03:09:29Z. The best-fitting in-scope technique is T1003.001 (LSASS Memory); the other technique labels (T1056.004, T1110.002, T1212, T1555, T1556, T1558) are alternative interpretations of the same events, and F15/F21 explicitly note no cracking or exploitation was observed.

title: SAM_SERVER and SamSs registry handles requested by lsass.exe on scranton
rationale: Security 4656 events show handles to the SAM object (SAM_SERVER, AccessMask 0xf003f) and to the SamSs service registry key requested by lsass.exe on scranton.dmevals.local; this is the SAM credential-dumping technique, assessed suspicious/low confidence.

title: Hardcoded plaintext passwords in attacker PowerShell tooling on SCRANTON
rationale: Script blocks contain hardcoded plaintext secrets ('saribas', 'lolol', 'MyCozyPassw0rd!') used by the attacker tooling, combined with the credential file sweep and certificate export — unsecured credentials in attacker tooling on a compromised host.

title: Recursive user-profile sweep for password/login-named files archived to Draft.Zip on SCRANTON
rationale: PowerShell recursively enumerated the user profile for *psw*/*pass*/*login*/*admin*/*vpn files and archived them to Draft.Zip — searching user files for stored credentials (Credentials In Files).

title: PowerShell Get-PrivateKeys exported LocalMachine certificate private keys to .pfx on SCRANTON
rationale: All describe the same Get-PrivateKeys script block (from readme.ps1) enumerating cert:\LocalMachine and exporting every certificate with a private key to a password-protected .pfx in pbeesly's Downloads, later staged into OfficeSupplies.7z. The best-fitting in-scope technique is T1552.004 (Private Keys); T1649 is an alternative label for the same action.

title: SMB/RPC/WinRM traffic carried by spoofed MAC and NetBIOS name-service broadcasts
rationale: The poisoned L2 path carries SMB/RPC/WinRM toward 10.0.1.6 and NetBIOS name-service broadcasts are on the wire, positioning the attacker for name-resolution poisoning/SMB relay; no relayed authentication is directly proven, so assessed suspicious.

title: ARP cache poisoning: second MAC impersonating 10.0.1.4
rationale: A second MAC (fc:bd:67:e1:a9:c1) appears as orig_l2_addr for source IP 10.0.1.4 interleaved with the legitimate NIC MAC — ARP cache poisoning.

title: PsExec reuse of known pbeesly credentials to move to NASHUA
rationale: The 4648 explicit-credential events pair with PsExec64.exe run on scranton.dmevals.local using the cleartext pbeesly password to launch python.exe on NASHUA; no password spraying occurred. This is remote-service lateral movement, not credential access.

title: Suspicious .scr and python.exe payloads opening full-access handles to conhost/cmd/powershell
rationale: The observed action is execution of a malicious screen-saver and dropped python.exe payloads that open 0x1FFFFF handles to console/shell processes; this is process execution/injection behavior rather than credential access, so it is out of scope.
